subject: MedScale discovery: model fit recap, benchmarks & quantization tradeoffs
messages:

Subject: Follow-up: MedScale model-fit & throughput discussion

Thanks Mina & Connor — good call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a couple asks so we can move to a quick POC: 

- Goal: real-time clinical note summarization (avg 180 tokens in / 120 tokens out) with error tolerance <= 1.5% hallucination on key-entity extraction.
- Primary constraints: sub-200ms p95 latency target for single-inference flows, and backend throughput ~120 qps during peak batch windows.
- Security: SOC2 compliance required (we can provide the security contact once we kick off).

Could you send: recommended model variants (incl quantization options), any benchmark runs we can review, and a sample prompt set for our core workflows? Also concerned about quality regressions if we use aggressive quantization — any initial thoughts?

I attached the call recording for reference. Proposed next call: Tue Nov 9, 10am PT for a 1-hr kickoff/POC planning.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Chen
Head of Platform
MedScale AI

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: MedScale model-fit & throughput discussion

Sam — thanks for the clear summary and for the recording. High-level answers and next steps below. I kept technical detail in the body for your engineers and included an initial recommendation set plus links to bench results and the prompt set.

Quick recommendation (priority order for POC):
1) Llama-3-70B (AWQ 4-bit profile) — best balance of conversational fidelity + large-context stability for entity extraction. Expect ~25–30% CPU/GPU token-cost savings vs fp16 with minimal quality regression on our heldout prompts.
2) Mistral-Instruct-13B (GPTQ 4-bit) — very cost-effective for short-turn summarization; watch for occasional verbatim truncation on long clinical phrases.
3) Redstone-13B (FP8) — strong throughput on our recent FP8 kernels; quality comparable to fp16 on average but slightly noisier on rare entity edge cases.

Tradeoffs summary: AWQ tends to preserve instruction-following and is conservatively robust on KV-cache retention; GPTQ can be smaller/faster but sometimes shows tokenization artifacts on rare medical terms; FP8 delivers highest throughput with modest quality variance on out-of-distribution phrasing. See attached tradeoffs spreadsheet for numbers and a simple decision matrix.

Benchmarks & artifacts:
- Prompt set: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-medscale-promptsets (medscale-promptset-v1.jsonl attached)
- Benchmark run: https://bench.redwood.ai/run/8f3a2b-medscale-20261102 (includes p50/p95/p99, token-cost breakdown, and eval slices)
- Tradeoff doc: tradeoffs_awq_gptq_fp8.xlsx (attached)

Proposed short-term plan:
- POC kickoff (Nov 9): agree success metrics + load profile, spin up a canary with 1 GPU pool for the 13B variant and a 2-GPU pool for 70B AWQ.
- Week 0: smoke tests + prompt tuning; Week 1: throughput tuning + quality gating; Week 2: rollout and monitoring.

Next steps for your team: confirm kickoff time, and please share your SOC2 contact (we'll provide our evidence link).

Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: medscale-promptset-v1.jsonl, tradeoffs_awq_gptq_fp8.xlsx

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Follow-up: MedScale model-fit & throughput discussion

Looping Laura in — couple technical notes from our runtime team after eyeballing the benchmarks Mina linked: 

> On Mon, Nov 2, 2026 at 10:05 Mina Haddad wrote:
> > Tradeoffs summary: AWQ tends to preserve instruction-following and is conservatively robust on KV-cache retention; GPTQ can be smaller/faster but sometimes shows tokenization artifacts on rare medical terms; FP8 delivers highest throughput with modest quality variance on out-of-distribution phrasing.

Runtime/ops comments:
- AWQ 4-bit on the 70B shows good p95 latency for single-stream requests on a 2xA100-80GB profile when we enable continuous batching up to ~8 concurrent streams. KV-cache retention tests look stable across 8k context windows in our bench.
- GPTQ 4-bit (13B) is performant but we saw a ~0.6% drop in exact-match for entity extraction on a 2k sample of the medscale prompts — worth surfacing to the customer as a potential regression risk.
- FP8 path (13B) on our newest kernels reduces token cost by ~38% vs fp16 but requires tuned decoder temp and additional prompt normalization to avoid hallucinations on abbreviations.

Ops ask for POC plan:
- Canary rollout: start with 10% traffic to AWQ-70B (read-only validation flows) + 80% to 13B variants; watch exact-match slices for entity extraction.
- Monitoring hooks: create alert when entity-extract exact-match drops >0.8% vs baseline or when p95 > 220ms.

Connor

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Follow-up: MedScale model-fit & throughput discussion

Agreed on Connor's ops recommendations. I'll throw in a short canary checklist to include in the kickoff deck: 

1) Config: AWQ-70B pool (2 GPUs) + Mistral-13B-GPTQ pool (1 GPU) + Redstone-13B-FP8 as a burst option.
2) Autoscale thresholds: scale out if p50 latency > 120ms for 30s rolling window or CPU utilisation > 70% for 1 minute.
3) Fallback policy: if quality alert fires (>0.8% EM drop) automatically route to AWQ-70B for that route; log output and trigger immediate human review.
4) Cost estimate (rough): under expected traffic profile, FP8 baseline yields ~35% cost reduction vs fp16; AWQ-70B will be ~1.6x cost of 13B GPTQ but should be used for critical entity-extract pipelines.

I'll prepare a short Ops SLA slide and a canary runbook for Nov 9.

Laura 
Head of Solutions Ops, Redwood Inference

- Initial model matrix for canary: Mistral-13B-GPTQ (primary), Redstone-13B-FP8 (burst), Llama-3-70B-AWQ (golden fallback for failing routes).
